long_biography.plain_text:
Građa predates Mijić, having been founded in Solin in 1954. By the mid-2000s he controlled the merchant, which expanded from construction materials into a broad home-improvement range and a seven-centre coastal network. He has remained involved through ownership and management roles, and now solely owns Građa–Prodajni centri.

Alongside his brother Matko, Mijić developed property and tourism holdings around Split and the Dalmatian coast. A 2023 reorganisation divided the older group’s inventories and most employees between two operating companies, sharpening his direct role in the sales-centre business. His portfolio also includes a boat-leasing company, but construction-materials retail remains the clearest long-running commercial platform.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 94. The authoritative Croatian Josip Mijic and Renata record aligns with a public Renata-to-Kanga name history, an official Kanga-to-Superyachts J.&P. reference and official FINA records naming Josip Mijić as that Split yacht-leasing company's sole member and manager. FINA independently ties the same exact name and geography to Građa–Prodajni centri, and the yacht company's public Građa-branded contact provides a further collision bridge. Numerous Croatian and international namesakes were excluded because they lacked this combined vessel, company, business and geography pattern.

No reviewed public page directly says that Josip Mijić personally owns Renata. The person-to-vessel conclusion therefore depends on the authoritative owner record plus the Renata/Kanga, Kanga/Superyachts J.&P. and Superyachts J.&P./Mijić chain. This indirect final bridge keeps identity confidence below 95.

Official and reliable Croatian sources consistently use Josip Mijić, while the authoritative input uses the ASCII-normalised Josip Mijic. Display name and surname corrections restore the canonical diacritic spelling without changing the resolved identity.

Wealth origin is classified as broad Self-made under the amended reasonable-inference policy. Građa predates Mijić, so he is not its founder, but contemporary reporting documents his contribution of the Opuzen sales centre in a capital increase and cash acquisition of the remaining minority shares, followed by continued ownership, management and expansion. The source of his earlier capital and initial controlling stake remains unresolved, so neither Self-made independent nor Self-made advantaged is supportable; no inheritance or family-transfer mechanism is evidenced.

Fashion & Retail is the closest approved broad industry value for Građa's construction-materials wholesale, retail and home-improvement network. The approved Construction materials tag provides the necessary sector precision; the broad field does not imply an apparel business.

Operator is used because official records show Mijić currently owns and manages Građa–Prodajni centri and reporting documents his long control of the operating group. Founder is excluded because the original Građa enterprise was established decades before his documented involvement.

Property and tourism are evidenced as secondary parts of a wider portfolio, while Superyachts J.&P. is a vessel-leasing company. Neither displaces Građa as the clearest long-running wealth platform, so no Real Estate, Hotels, Tourism or Maritime tag is assigned.

The authoritative input records Renata at 499 GT and YachtHunter matches that figure, whereas SuperYacht Times reports 479 GT. The discrepancy may reflect measurement or refit differences, but it is unresolved and appears only in research notes rather than the biographies.

The current Renata relationship begins in 2019, one year after the vessel's reported 2018 launch. Public sources reviewed do not explain the precise acquisition date, transfer structure or the Kanga-to-Renata renaming, so those details are not narrated.

The existing Instagram URL uses the high-collision handle josipmijic18 and could not be independently tied to the Građa and Superyachts J.&P. owner. It is preserved only in the immutable input snapshot and is not used as evidence, duplicated as a proposal or relied upon for any personal fact.

No collision-safe LinkedIn or personal website was found. Građa's official site is proposed as a Company Website; no Forbes profile, birth details, middle names, second nationality, birthplace, birth country, secondary residence or private net worth could be verified.

Company financial results and employee counts are not treated as Mijić's personal wealth. Both biographies are sale-independent and source-invisible, omit Renata and Kanga, and avoid a claim about how the Građa stake was acquired.
